newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli defence minister says tunnel timing bad.
newsitem.headline: Israeli defence minister says tunnel timing bad.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai criticised on Tuesday the timing of the opening of a tunnel in Jerusalem that sparked Israeli-Palestinian gunbattles and clashes last week.
It was the third time Mordechai had expressed doubts about the action by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"We have the right to open it when we decide to open it," Mordechai told Israel's army radio.
"The principal problem, in my opinion, was the issue of the timing because timing has meaning," he said.

The tunnel, near Moslem sites in Arab East Jerusalem, caused long-simmering anger at Netanyahu's foot-dragging on implementing Palestinian self-rule, to boil over, Palestinians say. The clashes killed 57 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers.

Last week Mordechai said that perhaps the government had not taken everything into consideration when opening the archaeological tunnel adjacent to al-Aqsa mosque. This week he was quoted as saying he knew the tunnel was to be opened only several hours beforehand.
